issues.legal_issue: A collective compensation rate does not bind an owner who did not consent to it.
material_facts: A committee recorded that landowners had agreed on a compensation rate, but the owner did not participate in the meeting.
The authorities did not produce an individual written agreement in the prescribed form or establish that notice of the meeting had been served on the owner.
The owner later asked for reasonable and adequate compensation and sought copies of any agreement.
issues.conclusion: The owner had not consented to the committee’s compensation rate and was not bound by it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 29(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, compensation may be paid according to an agreement between the government and the person to be compensated. Rule 10(b) of the Karnataka Land Acquisition Rules, 1965 requires the agreement to be in Form D. A committee’s recorded consensus does not establish an individual owner’s agreement where the prescribed written agreement is absent and service of notice to that owner is not established.

rule.if: acquisition_under_special_industrial_law and collective_rate_recorded and (individual_written_agreement_absent or meeting_notice_service_unproved)

predicates.acquisition_under_special_industrial_law: The government acquired land through a special law governing development of industrial areas.
predicates.collective_rate_recorded: A committee recorded a compensation rate as having been agreed to by landowners collectively.
predicates.individual_written_agreement_absent: The authorities did not produce a written agreement showing that the particular owner accepted the compensation rate.
predicates.meeting_notice_service_unproved: The authorities did not establish that notice of the compensation meeting was served on the particular owner.

issues.definition: When land is acquired through a special industrial-area law and a collective rate is recorded, an owner is not bound by that rate if no individual written agreement exists or service of notice to that owner is unproved.

issues.legal_issue: The time-based lapse provisions of the general land acquisition laws do not cause an acquisition under a special industrial development law to lapse where the land vests by final declaration independently of an award.
material_facts: The acquisition proceeded under a special industrial development law, under which land vested in the State upon publication of the final declaration.
No compensation award was made for the owners’ land, and the owners did not receive the compensation.
The authorities deposited compensation in court in light of a dispute about who was entitled to receive it.
The High Court applied the later general land acquisition law’s lapse provision to quash the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition had not lapsed under the general land acquisition laws; the High Court’s decision quashing it was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 28(4) and 28(5) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act provide for vesting upon publication of the final declaration, independently of an award. Section 11A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 does not apply to acquisitions under that special law, as held in M. Nagabhushana v. State of Karnataka, (2011) 3 SCC 408. The Court relied on the related reasoning in Pratap v. State of Rajasthan, (1996) 3 SCC 1; Munithimmaiah v. State of Karnataka, (2002) 4 SCC 326; Offshore Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Bangalore Development Authority, (2011) 3 SCC 139; and Girnar Traders (3) v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 3 SCC 1. Because the special law is a self-contained code and the general law’s award-time provision does not apply, Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 does not make such an acquisition lapse. The Court also applied the incorporation principle in State of M.P. v. M.V. Narasimhan, (1975) 2 SCC 377; it distinguished Mariyappa v. State of Karnataka, (1998) 3 SCC 276, because the legislation there was not a self-contained code.

predicates.acquisition_under_special_industrial_law: The proceeding is an acquisition of land under a special law governing development of industrial areas.
predicates.land_vested_on_final_declaration: The governing law made the land vest in the State upon publication of the final declaration, independently of an award.
predicates.award_not_made: The authority had not made an award determining compensation for the land.

issues.definition: When a special industrial-area acquisition vests land upon final declaration and no award has been made, the acquisition does not lapse merely because the award is absent.

issues.legal_issue: When an owner has not agreed to compensation in a special industrial-area acquisition, the authorities must continue the compensation process under the special acquisition scheme rather than quash the acquisition.
material_facts: The owner did not agree to the compensation rate recorded by the advisory committee.
The authorities had not made an award determining compensation for the owner’s land.
The first-instance court had permitted the authorities to determine compensation under the special law, but the appellate court instead quashed the acquisition.
The Supreme Court restored the direction to fix compensation under the special law.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition remained in force, and the authorities were directed to fix compensation under the special law, proceeding by agreement or, if no agreement could be reached, by reference for determination.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 29(2) and 29(3) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act provide for compensation by agreement and, if agreement cannot be reached, reference to the Deputy Commissioner for determination. Section 30 applies the procedure of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 to the inquiry, award, court reference, apportionment, and payment of compensation. The absence of an agreement therefore requires the statutory compensation determination to proceed; it does not invalidate or lapse the acquisition.

predicates.acquisition_under_special_industrial_law: The proceeding is an acquisition of land under a special law governing development of industrial areas.
predicates.individual_owner_not_consented: The particular owner did not agree to the compensation proposed by the authorities.
predicates.compensation_award_absent: The authority had not made an award determining compensation for the owner’s land.

issues.definition: If an owner has not agreed to compensation and no award has been made in a special industrial-area acquisition, compensation must be determined under that acquisition scheme.
